newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank chief sees 9-10 pct growth in 96. [CORRECTED 10:36 GMT]
newsitem.headline: China central bank chief sees 9-10 pct growth in 96. [CORRECTED 10:36 GMT]

text.p: China should report economic growth of 9-10 percent this year, with retail price inflation below 6.6 percent, a central bank spokesman quoted central bank governor Dai Xianglong as saying.

(Corrects rate of growth in headline and first paragraph from 12 percent. A central bank spokesman told Reuters that the official China Securities newspaper had misquoted the central bank governor. Corrects attribution of new forecast to a bank spokesman quoting the governor.)
China's gross domestic product rose by 10.2 percent in 1995 and retail inflation reached 14.8 percent.
China's official target for inflation for 1996 is 10 percent but it has since said that it expected inflation to be around 6.5 percent.

The governor of the People's Bank of China, or central bank, was quoted as saying that policies aimed at controlling inflation were showing results and they had produced an obvious slowing of money supply growth.
Dai made the remarks at a financial seminar on Monday.
